evidence: tens of thousands of people have been forced to flee their homes
In neighboring Spain, fires continued to consume areas west and north of the capital Madrid, where tens of thousands of people have been forced to flee their homes.

nary_nodes.label: Road and train disruptions near Bordeaux
evidence: Fires near Bordeaux have also blocked roads, including a highway along the Atlantic coast, and halted train service
Fires near Bordeaux have also blocked roads, including a highway along the Atlantic coast, and halted train service near the major wine producing city.

nary_nodes.label: Deployment of firefighters, military, and police
evidence: Some 2,500 firefighters as well as 1,500 military personnel and 1,200 police have been deployed to the region.

nary_nodes.label: Total displacements in France
evidence: New overnight evacuations brought the total number of displacements in France to over 220,000.

nary_nodes.label: Total burned area in France
evidence: the fires have consumed some 42,000 hectares (103,000 acres)
In all, the fires have consumed some 42,000 hectares (103,000 acres).

nary_nodes.label: Burned area compared to Paris and Manhattan
evidence: an area four times the size of Paris, or seven times the size of Manhattan

nary_nodes.label: Largest burned area since 1949
evidence: laying waste to more land than at any time since 1949, when fires destroyed 50,000 hectares.

nary_nodes.label: Evacuations in Var region
evidence: Separately, firefighters are battling an active fire in the southern Var region, where 3,000 people have been evacuated.

nary_nodes.label: Population of Bordeaux
evidence: Fires near Bordeaux — a city of 268,000 residents — have also blocked roads.

nary_nodes.label: Nunez on Gironde fire intensity
evidence: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez on Sunday said that the blaze raging in the Gironde region near popular Bordeaux had become 'extremely intense and unpredictable again' overnight.

nary_nodes.label: Sanchez on difficult hours ahead
evidence: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Sunday said, 'difficult hours lie ahead' as he toured areas impacted by fire west of the capital, before adding 'positive' developments had been seen in containing the fire overnight.
